summary.text: 贵 is the simplified form of 貴, whose traditional dictionary gloss is “not cheap”; current meanings include “expensive” and “valuable.” The traditional graph is analyzed as a compound, though its early components are disputed.

formation.text: The traditional dictionary analysis treats 貴 as phonosemantic: 貝 connects the graph with shells and money, while 臾 supplies a sound cue. Another account describes early forms as hands holding earth and assigns the sound role to 中. The early graph’s depiction and sound element remain disputed; 贵 is the simplified counterpart of 貴.

components.text: In 貴, 貝 links the graph to shells used as currency and thus to money and value. This analysis does not by itself establish that the early graph depicted hands carrying a shell.

The traditional dictionary and a scholarly analysis identify 臾 as the sound component in 貴; the dictionary associates it with an ancient form of 蕢, described in the study as the protoform of 簣. The exact historical sound correspondence is incompletely established.

sound_limitation.text: These analyses identify 臾 as phonetic, but do not provide a complete comparative series establishing its historical sound relation to 貴. The reported reconstructions are proposals, not recorded ancient speech.

sound.text: A study reports these Old Chinese reconstructions in Zhengzhang Shangfang’s system. They provide a proposed sound comparison, not a record of ancient pronunciation; the study reports a different reconstruction for 貴 in another system.

components.text: A competing account describes early forms as hands holding earth and assigns 中 the sound role, in contrast with the 貝-plus-臾 analysis.

sound_limitation.text: The cited account calls 中 phonetic but supplies no reading comparison establishing its sound relation to 貴.

history.text: References present oracle-bone, bronze, seal, and standard forms, but the descriptions do not settle the details of the early graph. The later variant 䝿 is described as a regularization of a small-seal form; other transmitted spellings include possible graphic distortions.
贵 is the simplified counterpart of 貴, with 貝 written as 贝. The adoption date of this particular simplified form is unresolved.

uncertainties.text: The early graphic analysis is disputed: one account describes hands holding earth and assigns 中 the sound role, while the traditional dictionary and scholarly analysis identify 貝 and 臾. The available accounts do not resolve the original depiction or sound element.
The chronology connecting price, social rank, worth, esteem, and honor is not established by independently dated primary-text examples.

senses.text: A transmitted dictionary glosses 貴 as “not cheap”; current dictionary records also give “expensive” and “costly.” The dating of this sense in primary texts is unresolved.
Current dictionary records include “valuable” and “precious.” Their dating and whether they developed directly from “expensive” are unresolved.
Dictionary records include esteem, honor, and high social status. Their chronology and semantic path from the price sense are unresolved.

limitations.text: The transmitted gloss “not cheap” and current senses are supported, but a dated sequence among them is not. Reported classical examples have not been verified against primary texts.

overview.text: 贵 is the simplified form of 貴, whose traditional dictionary gloss is “not cheap”; today it commonly means “expensive” or “valuable.” The traditional graph is analyzed as a sound-and-meaning compound, though accounts differ about its early components.

components.text: In 貴, 貝 connects the graph with shells used as money and their association with value.
The cited reconstruction compares 臾 and 貴 through a shared proposed sound pattern; this comparison does not settle the disputed analysis.
An alternative account describes hands holding earth and assigns 中 the sound role; this analysis is disputed.

relationships.text: In the traditional dictionary analysis of 貴, 貝 contributes an association with money and value.
The traditional dictionary and scholarly analysis identify 臾 as the sound element in 貴; the competing early graphic analysis remains unresolved.
An alternative paleographic account assigns 中 the sound role in 貴, differing from the 臾 analysis.
贵 is the simplified form of 貴, including 贝 for 貝.
